implementationTested: Production Chrome H.264 decode and Theora encode using the published within-theora Wasm, followed by quota-preflighted OPFS staging and a single backpressured 256 KiB copy to the selected destination.

output.identity: Identical to the independently decoded 1,560-frame Ogg/Theora output in the earlier candidate evidence, not an extension rename.

formula: peak complete Chrome process-tree private memory during conversion minus stable clean blank-Chrome process-tree private memory

coldRuns.testFailure: The 8.8 MB staged final copy completed before Playwright could click Cancel; this is a cancellation-checkpoint race, not a conversion or output failure.

diagnosis: Both sessions had similar absolute peak process-tree private memory (506.047 versus 507.199 MiB), but the second stable clean blank-Chrome baseline was about 22.773 MiB lower, so the required formula exposed 264.445 MiB. The renderer and GPU process accounted for most of the growth. A favorable single cold run cannot override the failing repeat. The staged path also took about 34 seconds rather than the earlier roughly 22-second MP4 candidate, so it was not kept as an optimization.
decision: Revert MP4-specific staging code and keep mp4-to-ogv failed/hidden. Keep the selective deterministic fixture-generation option because it avoids generating an unrelated 147 MB MOV. Preserve the older direct-memory rejection separately in evidence/mp4-to-ogv-candidate-2026-09-15.json.
cleanup: After compacting this evidence, delete the generated project-local 147 MB MP4, converted copies, and this cycle's raw JSON/CSV/HTML reports; retain the tracked fixture manifest, the older 2026-09-19 diagnostic report, and protected test.mkv unchanged.
